verdict: Lend selectively in Silvassa electrical equipment, pumps and motors — pursue export-ready component makers with tight working-capital control, avoid leveraged domestic-only pump assemblers until margin and receivable data are verified.
title: Silvassa Electrical Equipment, Pumps & Motors: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**These units buy steel, copper, laminations, castings and bought-out electronics, then convert them into motors, pumps, switchgear and components sold to OEMs, projects and export buyers.** Cash comes in on dispatch, but the gap between paying for metal and collecting from the buyer is where the risk sits. **Pricing power is thin in standard pumps and stronger in custom/specialty motors and railway, wind and off-highway applications** [4]. So when a proposal lands, check whether the order book is standard catalogue volume or engineered-to-order; if it is standard, ask what stops the buyer from switching on price.

## Where value and cash sit now
**The national demand signal is strong: IIP NIC 27 output is +30.9% YoY and +28.5% Apr-to-date** [D]. **Exports are +19.8% Apr-to-date in USD** [D]. But **bank credit to the space is growing +37.7% YoY against +28.5% output, a +9.2 pp gap** [D] — some of that lending is funding working capital stretch, not just growth. Peer evidence is mixed: Shakti Pumps grew Q1 FY27 revenue 37.9% YoY to Rs 858.67 crore while PAT fell 46.72% to Rs 51.59 crore [7], and H1 FY27 revenue rose 24.5% YoY to Rs 16,047 Mn with PAT down to Rs 90.10 crore from Rs 187.54 crore [5]. **Growth is real; margin and cash conversion are not keeping pace.** Rating reports on this space flag high working-capital intensity and large capex-plus-working-capital build [8][9].

## The Silvassa opportunity
**Local sources are thin — the main Silvassa item is a U.T.-level FTA outreach programme to strengthen exports** [1]; the other local hits are topic pages with no usable operating data [2][3]. So lean on first principles and peers. **Pursue component and sub-assembly makers supplying export OEMs, specialty-motor makers with engineered order books, and units adding FTA-linked export lines** [1][4]. **Avoid domestic-only pump assemblers bidding government tenders on thin margins, and any unit whose growth is funded by receivables ageing rather than cash.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure limits around the working-capital cycle, not turnover.** Take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, monthly bank statements, and quarterly GSTR-2B versus purchase reconciliation. **Ask for receivable days and inventory days by customer; if either is rising while sales grow, ask which buyer is stretching and cap exposure to that buyer.** For capex, insist on promoter equity first — peers raised Rs 290 crore in FY2025 and Rs 210 crore in May 2025 to support capex and working capital [8]. **Covenant on debt/EBITDA and current ratio, and take a monthly stock statement plus quarterly CMA data.**

## Early-warning signs
- **Receivable days rising two quarters running** -> freeze enhancement, ask for buyer-wise ageing.
- **PAT falling while revenue rises** (as in Shakti Pumps [5][7]) -> reprice or reduce limit.
- **Inventory build without matching orders** -> ask for order book and dispatch register.
- **Promoter equity not infused against stated capex** -> hold disbursement.
watch: Receivable days up two quarters -> freeze enhancement and seek buyer-wise ageing
Input credit mismatch above 5% -> ask for explanation and cap limit
Debt/EBITDA above agreed covenant -> reprice or reduce limit
Cash receipts lagging dispatches -> ask which buyer is delaying and cap exposure
